image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Approach above the live red gear with open fingers, correcting to a vertical grasp orientation; position estimated from RGB.
Descend vertically toward the centered red hub, retaining the open grasp aperture.
Fine-center over the red hub, lower the hand to grasp height, then close the fingers around its neck.
Lift the closed grasp straight up and inspect whether the red gear stays between the fingers.
The red gear remains in the grasp. Carry it above the vacant base peg, leaving vertical clearance for alignment.
Lower toward the vacant peg with a small lateral alignment correction, keeping the gear firmly held.
Gently lower the aligned red gear onto the peg to the assembly height, watching for seating or obstruction.
Hold assembly height and begin a small axial turn to check engagement and help the red gear seat on the base.
Continue a controlled axial rotation while keeping the gear at the peg height; inspect the pair for engagement.
Turn the held red gear further about the base axis, maintaining the seated height and closed fingers.
Continue the axial turn with a gentle 3 mm descent to improve seating; engagement remains visually uncertain.
The gear may be perched rather than fully seated. Lift for clearance and return to a neutral orientation to realign the bore.
Lower over the peg and gently release to let the gear settle flat, since its bore appears tilted in the grasp.
Withdraw with open fingers so the released gear can settle and its alignment on the pin can be checked.
The released gear appears supported above its seated plane. Regrasp its hub to correct the small bore-to-pin offset.
Lift the regrasped gear clear of the base to expose the peg and compare its center with the bore.
The gear was not retained and is tilted on the pin. Descend farther around its neck, slightly recentering, then reclose.
Secure the lower neck grasp, then lift to verify retention and clear the locating pin.
The gear is now retained. Lower carefully toward the newly exposed pin, preserving the corrected lateral alignment.
Nudge the bore slightly toward the visible pin center while descending slowly to seat the gear.
Corrected the rejected tensor; lift clear and shift the held bore toward the pin. No compensation for the rejected call.
Align the bore laterally with the exposed pin and lower in small increments for another seating attempt.
The gear appears obstructed and tilted rather than seated. Lift clear before correcting the grasp and alignment.
The lifted gear is retained and approximately level. Return vertically toward the pin while preserving its current alignment.
Continue a slow vertical insertion below the previous stopping height; the regrasp holds the gear higher relative to the hand.
At the lower seating height, begin a gentle axial turn to engage and drive the paired gear.
Continue turning with a small hand-position compensation for the off-center grasp, aiming to rotate about the pin rather than displace the gear.
Continue the compensated axial turn at the lower assembly height, checking whether the paired gear is driven.
The red gear still appears slightly above the matching gear plane. Lower another centimeter gradually with a small aligning twist.
Release and withdraw to check whether the gear settles flat on the base rather than remaining tilted in the off-center grasp.
The released gear now appears flat at the base height. Center the open hand above its hub and reset yaw for a cleaner turning grasp.
Descend around the now-flat gear hub and close a centered grasp at the reference turning height.
The bore is now centered between the fingers and the gear appears flat. Start a slow axial turn without translating the hub.
Continue rotating the centered red hub at fixed height to drive the meshed gear pair.
Continue the steady axial turn while keeping the assembled gear centered and seated.
Extend the centered turn to increase rotation of the engaged pair without lifting the red gear.
Maintain a secure centered grasp and continue the axial turn beyond a quarter revolution, keeping the gear on its pin.
Release after the centered turn and withdraw vertically to verify that the red gear remains assembled and the pair is unobstructed.
The gear remains flat on the base. Recenter above its hub and unwind the empty wrist for another controlled driving turn.
Lower the recentered open fingers around the seated red hub, finish the wrist reset, and close for a secure turning grasp.
